title: Complete Tenses Review
description: Full tense review for Grade 10 boards (CBSE/ICSE): all twelve tenses, time markers, tense in context and tense shifts — with bilingual notes, exam-style practice and tests.

topics.title: The 12-Tense Map & Time Markers
topics.concept:
Every tense combines a time (present/past/future) with an aspect (simple/continuous/perfect/perfect continuous). Learn each with its signal words:

TenseSignal words
Simple Presentalways, usually, every day, never
Present Continuousnow, at the moment, look!, listen!
Present Perfectjust, already, yet, ever, since, for
Present Perfect Cont.since, for, all day, how long
Simple Pastyesterday, ago, last…, in 2019
Past Continuouswhile, as, at 8 p.m. yesterday
Past Perfectbefore, after, by the time, already
Future Simpletomorrow, next…, soon
Future Perfectby + future time, by then

Spot the marker → pick the tense. This single habit solves most exam gap-fills.

was cooking — 'while' + an interrupted past action → past continuous.

recap: 12 tenses = 4 aspects × 3 times; the helping verb carries the tense
Each tense has signal words (since/for, while, by the time…)
Spot the marker → choose the tense

topics.title: Tense in Context & Consistency
topics.concept:
In a passage, tenses must stay consistent unless the time genuinely changes. A sudden, unmotivated shift is an error.

  • ❌ She opened the door and walks in. → ✓ She opened the door and walked in.

Sequence of tenses: after a past main verb, the subordinate clause usually shifts to the past too:

  • He said that he was tired. (not 'is')
  • Exception — a universal truth stays present: She told us that the earth is round.

Tense in formal writing: reports often use the past or present perfect for findings (It was found that…), while general statements use the simple present (Pollution affects health).

examples.problem: Fix the shift: He entered the hall and sees his friend.
examples.solution: He entered the hall and saw his friend. — keep the narrative in the past.

examples.problem: Choose: The teacher said that water ___ (boil) at 100°C.
examples.solution: boils — a universal truth stays in the present even after a past reporting verb.

recap: Keep tenses consistent in a passage; avoid unmotivated shifts
After a past main verb, the subordinate clause usually shifts back
Universal truths stay in the present

questions.q: 'She ___ TV now.'
'They ___ to Agra last week.'
'I ___ my keys; I can't find them.'
'By the time you read this, I ___.'
'While she ___, the phone rang.'
'He ___ here for five years.' (still here)
'When we reached, the match ___.'
Universal truth: 'The teacher said that the moon ___ the earth.'
Fix: 'He entered and looks around.'
'I ___ for an hour when she came.'
'We ___ dinner at 8 every night.'
'By next year she ___ school.'
Choose the correct option: 'No sooner ___ the bell rung than the students rushed out.'
questions.explanation: 'No sooner had … than …' uses the past perfect with inversion.

questions.q: Fill in correctly: 'It ___ since morning, and the streets ___ still wet.'
Edit: 'By the time the ambulance will arrive, the patient will have recovered.'
questions.explanation: A time clause uses the present: 'By the time the ambulance arrives'.

questions.q: Choose the correct sequence: 'She was sure that she ___ the right decision.'
questions.explanation: Earlier than the past 'was' → past perfect 'had made'.

questions.q: Which sentence is free of tense error?
options: He has finished the work yesterday.
He had finished the work yesterday at 5.
He was finished the work yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'yesterday' with a single action → simple past 'finished'.

questions.q: Complete: 'Hardly had I closed my eyes ___ the alarm rang.'
Choose: 'The committee ___ the report by the end of this week.'
questions.explanation: Completed before a future point → future perfect.

questions.q: Identify the correctly sequenced sentence.
options: After he had eaten, he will sleep.
After he had eaten, he slept.
After he eats, he had slept.
After he has eaten, he slept.

intro.en: The board exam tests tenses everywhere — in gap-filling, editing, and writing. This chapter pulls all twelve tenses into one clear map, pairs each with its time markers, and trains you to keep tense consistent in a paragraph. Get this right and you secure marks across the whole paper.
intro.hi: बोर्ड परीक्षा हर जगह tenses जाँचती है — gap-filling, editing और लेखन में। यह अध्याय सभी बारह tenses को एक स्पष्ट मानचित्र में लाता है, हर एक को उसके time markers से जोड़ता है, और अनुच्छेद में tense को एकसमान रखने का अभ्यास कराता है। इसे सही कर लें तो पूरे पेपर में अंक सुरक्षित।

real_life.situation:
A board gap-fill item:

Q: By the time the firefighters arrived, the house ___ (burn) down completely.

A: …had burned down completely.
real_life.why: 'By the time … arrived' signals an earlier past action, which needs the past perfect 'had burned'. Recognising the time marker instantly tells you the tense — that is the exam skill this chapter builds.

rule_box.formula: 4 aspects × 3 times = 12 tenses; the helping verb carries the tense
rule_box.example: She writes / wrote / will write; is/was/will be writing; has/had/will have written.

quick_test.q: Which tense pairs with the marker 'by the time he arrived'?
quick_test.explanation: 'By the time + past action' signals the earlier action in the past perfect.

common_mistakes.wrong: He opened the door and walks in.
common_mistakes.right: He opened the door and walked in.
When I reached, the train had left.
common_mistakes.note: The earlier past action needs the past perfect.
Back-shift after a past reporting verb.

fill_l2.instructions: Fill in the tense suggested by the time marker.

error_detection.sentence: When I came, she already left.
error_detection.correct: When I came, she had already left.

error_detection.sentence: She entered and sees the mess.
error_detection.correct: She entered and saw the mess.

sentence_correction.wrong: By next year I complete my degree.
sentence_correction.correct: By next year I will have completed my degree.

sentence_correction.wrong: He said the earth was flat. (universal truth)
sentence_correction.correct: He said the earth is round.

sentence_correction.wrong: While she was cooking, the bell rings.
sentence_correction.correct: While she was cooking, the bell rang.

rearrangement.jumbled: had / I / when / reached / left / the / train
rearrangement.answer: When I reached, the train had left.

rearrangement.jumbled: rises / the / east / sun / the / in
rearrangement.answer: The sun rises in the east.

reading.passage: By the time Riya reached the auditorium, the function had already begun. The choir was singing, and the audience was listening quietly. She had practised her speech for weeks, and she knew it by heart. "By the end of today," she thought, "I will have faced my biggest fear." The sun was setting as she walked onto the stage.

questions.q: Identify the past perfect verbs and explain why they are used.
questions.answer: 'had already begun' and 'had practised' — actions completed before another past moment (Riya reaching).

questions.q: Which tense is 'was singing', and what does it show?
questions.answer: Past continuous — an action in progress at that past moment.

questions.q: Why is 'I will have faced' used in her thought?
questions.answer: Future perfect — an action that will be completed before a future point (the end of today).

speaking: I have been studying since morning.
By the time we arrived, the train had left.
She was reading when I called.

Water boils at one hundred degrees.

writing.prompt: Write a short paragraph (5–6 sentences) narrating a past event, deliberately using the simple past, past continuous and past perfect with correct sequencing.
writing.example: I reached the station late. The train had already left. People were waiting on the platform. I had forgotten to check the time.

challenge.q: Choose the correct sequence: 'He told me that he ___ the project the previous week.'
challenge.explanation: An action earlier than the past report → past perfect 'had completed'.

options: She opens the door and saw a dog.
She opened the door and sees a dog.
She opened the door and saw a dog.

challenge.explanation: Both verbs in the simple past.

challenge.q: Choose: 'I ___ (wait) for two hours when the bus finally arrived.'
challenge.explanation: Duration before a past event → past perfect continuous.
